_comment:
The experiment graph — one card per proposal, and the only order-of-work truth. Ported from the arch-transplant skill's `references/experiment-graph.md`, whose version lived in a markdown design doc and whose seven invariants said "scan periodically" with nothing scanning. `scripts/explore/graph.py check` is that scanner; this file is what it reads.

A card is NOT a run. The arm that verifies a card is an ordinary training run in `stages/training/runs/`, cited here by `run_id` — same boundary `/data-curate` draws for a conversion and `adaptation` draws for a converter. Nothing in the explore stage executes.
_comment_corpus:
‼️ The scope guard, and the reason this is a top-level field rather than a per-card one. Every `premise_share` on every card must have been measured on THIS corpus. arch-transplant's hardest rule — never kill a proposal with a number measured on a different corpus — is unenforceable while the corpus is implicit, and it is the rule that cost the most: a share quoted from another corpus predicted 47% where this one measured 4.62%.

Same shape as a run's `cfg.data.dataset_id` + `split_seed`, and for the same reason MLClaw refuses to compare metrics across a non-equivalent `scope`. Changing it invalidates every `premise_share` in the file — `graph.py check` says so rather than letting the numbers ride.
_comment_base:
‼️ The code axis's scope guard, and the twin of `corpus` above. That one pins what every `premise_share` was measured on; this one pins what every arm's delta is measured AGAINST -- Stage 6's "the control must be re-run on today's code" has no referent once "today" differs per arm.

Why it is needed at all: MLClaw resolves ONE code path per stage (`run-mechanics.md -> Code snapshot`: `stages/<stage>/code/_source if exists else stages/<stage>/code`, and for `code_source.source: local` a single external directory acting as a soft link), while SKILL.md Stage 3 says to compute the ready set and open all of it at once. So parallel arms share a working tree BY CONSTRUCTION, and `code_snapshot.py` reads that tree at launch: with two ports half-written in it, arm A's `code_dirty.patch` carries arm B's edits. It applies cleanly, it reproduces exactly, and `variation_summary` cannot see it -- an uncommitted edit to a model file moves neither `runtime_params` nor `workload`.

The isolation is one `git worktree add` per arm; this field and each card's `tree` are the RECORD of it, which is the half nothing could hold before. `commit` is the round's base SHA, frozen when the round opens and not moved while an arm is in flight -- a winner merged mid-round redefines the control under every arm still running, and the flag combination it creates is one nobody ran. `repo_subdir` is the offset when `code_dir` is not the repo root, the same one `code_snapshot.py` records.

! Not duplicated into config.json. `corpus` is written in both places for a stated reason (the graph scopes shares, the stage launches arms); this has no second reader, and a copy with no reader is just a value with two authors.
_comment_nodes:
One entry per proposal. `id` is a queue number, STABLE AND NEVER REUSED — a killed card's number is not recycled, because cross-references would then point at a different proposal.

Card: {id, title, kind, state, premise, premise_share, criterion, guardrail, parent, depends_on, oracle_ceiling, kill_condition, tier, axes, run_id, result, verdict, conditional_on, killed_by, revive_if, history[], tree}

‼️ `tree` is where this arm's code was WRITTEN -- {branch, base, head, path} -- and it is required of the three kinds that write code (`port`, `original`, `task_driven`), never of a `measurement`. A branch name is as unrecyclable as a queue number and for the same reason: it is what a settled card's evidence resolves through, so pointing a second arm at it moves the ref and the first card's `head` stops naming anything. `graph.py set` refuses the collision.

‼️ `depends_on` entries say WHAT THEY BLOCK, because a bare id can only say "wait" and half of the real dependencies here were never about the schedule. `"N06"` (or `{"id":"N06","blocks":"launch"}`) holds the arm shut: the premise share is unmeasured, the parent ckpt does not exist, the code cannot be written yet. `{"id":"N06","blocks":"reading"}` holds NOTHING shut -- the arm opens now and its verdict comes out stamped `conditional_on: ["N06"]`, because what it needed from N06 was a value, not a verdict. The test: am I waiting for its CONCLUSION, or for one value / artifact / line of code? Only the first is `launch`. See references/experiment-graph.md -> TAKE.

‼️ A card missing any required field may not reach `ready`. That gate is the whole point of the draft state: an arm opened from an incomplete card produces a number nobody can adjudicate, and it costs GPU hours to find that out.
_comment_disputes:
When two cards in this graph disagree. Borrowed from ARA (arXiv:2604.24658) -> research-manager 'Contradiction trigger', and the rule is the whole mechanism: NEITHER RECORD IS OVERWRITTEN. Both sides get a `disputed_by` marker, an entry lands here naming the pair, and it stops -- adjudication is the researcher's.

Before this existed the graph could not hold the state. A new result contradicting a settled verdict left two options and both destroy the record: rewrite the old card (losing exactly what the next round reads) or say nothing.

Entry: {id, state, challenger, disputed, detail, tiers, outcome, note, opened_at, resolved_at}

! A LOWER-TIER CARD MAY NOT DISPUTE A HIGHER-TIER ONE. SKILL.md Stage 3.5 rule 2: a cheap check gives you a reason to CONTINUE, never a reason to reject. Most apparent contradictions between a short run and a controlled one are not disagreements -- they are incomparabilities, and adjudicating one as a disagreement is how a good result gets thrown away by a cheap probe. `graph.py dispute` refuses it.

Outcomes: `upheld` (the challenger is right; the disputed card keeps its verdict AND gains `superseded_by` -- marked, never rewritten) | `rejected` (the challenger is wrong; the disputed card is untouched) | `not_comparable` (they never conflicted).
_comment_delta:
The ONE key this card changes relative to its parent, declared before the arm opens. `graph.py check` diffs the run's `lineage.variation_summary` against it and refuses on any extra key: more than one key moved means no result can be attributed to any of them.

Evidenced by a real round: a baseline at AP50 26.76 was read against an arm at 7.88 and the 3.4x credited to the technique. Four unintended differences sat between them -- rot_aug_deg 0->15, num_points 40000->145000, no_thin_cloud on->off, warm_lr_epochs 9->4 -- plus 8 GPUs down to 1.

! THE GPU COUNT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR THE CHECK'S DESIGN. world_size lives in `workload`, not in `runtime_params`, so `variation_summary` cannot see it. A guard reading only that field would have cleared the very round it exists to prevent -- which is the RUBBER-STAMP shape: a check that reports the conclusion it was built to stop. So both fields are compared.
_comment_eval_setting:
{held_at, own} -- for an arm that changes what the CORRECT measurement setting is.

One-to-one matching needs no NMS, and it was being compared against one-to-many UNDER NMS. Holding the setting fixed makes the contrast clean and at the same time measures the setting rather than the technique. Both readings are needed and they answer different questions:

  at_held  the fair contrast -- same setting on both sides, so the delta is the technique
  at_own   what you would actually ship

! `at_own` IS FREE. It re-evaluates a checkpoint that already exists; no training. The arm that surfaced this read 84.16 held and 92.15 at its own setting, and reporting either alone would have been a different claim. `check` refuses a single number on such a card.
_comment_states:
Seven, and the split that matters is `filled` vs `closed` — HAVING A RESULT IS NOT HAVING A CONCLUSION. A card whose numbers are in but whose verdict is not is `filled`; treating it as `closed` propagates an unexplained number downstream as if it were a finding. The recorded instance: a mechanism criterion passed literally (the negatives did come back) while the verdict was that the mechanism checked out AND WAS NOT WORTH ANYTHING, and that verdict needed another card's measurement before it could be reached.

‼️ Three of the seven are DERIVED and four are DECLARED, and that split is load-bearing: the derived ones change when a DIFFERENT card settles, so a stored copy of them is stale the moment it is written. `graph.py` recomputes them at every read (`_derive_state`) and writes the field forward only as a courtesy to outside readers — never trust it over the derivation. Read it off the label instead and you get what this file used to produce: `status` reporting `blocked: 3` while `ready` handed out the same three cards as takeable.

DERIVED — a function of the card's fields plus its dependencies:
draft    ⬜ to fill in  — a one-line idea, schema incomplete
blocked  🟨 waiting    — card complete, dependencies unmet (and ONLY that — a complete card with no dependencies is 🟩, never 🟨)
ready    🟩 ready      — may open an arm

DECLARED — an act somebody performed; the record IS the declaration:
running  🔵 running    — a run is declared; `run_id` is set. ‼️ The `run_id` is what makes it running, not the label: a card carrying one and no result is treated as running even if the label was never flipped, because that is the shape that otherwise gets a second arm opened on it
filled   🟪 filled     — results on the card, VERDICT NOT YET REACHED
closed   ✅ closed     — conclusion reached; may be another card's dependency
killed   ❌ killed     — with `killed_by` + `revive_if`; ALSO may be a dependency ("stop waiting on this one")
_comment_provenance:
Who put this card on the queue: user | ai-suggested | ai-executed | user-revised. Borrowed from ARA (arXiv:2604.24658), whose Live Research Manager tags every entry the same four ways.

Load-bearing here because SKILL.md Stage 3 says this queue is maintained BY THE USER, not the agent's notebook: the user drops in a one-line idea, the agent completes the card and executes it. Without the tag, a card the user demanded and a card the agent invented are the same row -- and the round's whole ordering is supposed to be the user's.

‼️ `ai-suggested` never auto-upgrades. Only an explicit `set` moves it, because the entire value of the tag is that the agent's own confidence cannot earn it. Same rule as `/ask-human` refusing `verified` when nothing but the person confirmed it. The DISTRIBUTION is itself a quality signal, and `check` reports it.
_comment_killed_by:
Four deaths, and their `revive_if` are differently shaped — writing them interchangeably is the same as not writing them.

share_too_small     the fault is real but rare here     → revive on a new corpus / new operating condition
faithful_but_inert  ported correctly, changed nothing   → revive on a changed metric or changed upstream
wrong_mechanism     the proposal itself was wrong       → revive by measuring the effect DIRECTLY; the proxy condition need not hold
unfaithful_port     ‼️ NOT a death — go back and fix it → no revive_if; it returns to `running`

‼️ `revive_if` states a PROXY condition. A card revives the moment the effect is measured directly, whether or not the proxy fired — the recorded instance is a CDN card revived by direct measurement while neither of its two written revive_if conditions was ever met.
_comment_tier:
T0–T4 from the verification-budget axes. ‼️ The tier travels with every number this card produces, forever. A `[T1 trend]` conclusion may not be cited next week as a `[T2 controlled]` one — soft numbers being promoted to hard conclusions is the single most common way this pipeline dies, and it is how a false noise floor entered the record once already.

T0 not verified · T1 trend (short run/subset, noise floor NOT required) · T2 single controlled point (noise floor required) · T3 rides a full run · T4 cheap approximation, FOR PRICING ONLY — an approximation failing never refutes the original.
_comment_axes:
The three that decide the tier: V verification cost · P prior · U project value. Each high|medium|low.

‼️ V's main determinant is whether open-source code exists, not how many lines change: with only a paper you must first invent it and then spend a training run discovering the invention was wrong. `code_availability` is therefore recorded beside V, not folded into it.
_comment_invariants: What `graph.py check` enforces, and what each failure means. It REPORTS; it never repairs — a graph that repairs itself hides the fact that something wrote an illegal state.
